scope:
Unseeded Conway completion using a complete internal-star matching cover.

For each root line, partition its other six lines into the template's
components. A component of size 6s has 2s vertices in each star, so its
internal star has (2s-1)!! possible perfect matchings. Their Cartesian
product is exhaustive without any relabelling or automorphism assumption.
Choose the line with the smallest product. Only this one star is fixed;
the opposite matching, the cross permutation, and the Gram remain free.

This model uses no minimum-four table, frozen frontier, local P/M1 catalogue,
or Gram witness. A template is excluded only if every matching is excluded.
An INFEASIBLE CP-SAT verdict is not a portable UNSAT certificate.

coverage.scope: All star matchings modulo permitted root relabellings. The remaining edges are still variables; these cases are not complete graphs.

model.coverage_scope: One root component template; global coverage requires the source template cover.

triangles.scope:
Exact lambda=1 using actual triangle indicators, plus triangle cores.

A Gamma edge sharing a root label already has its common neighbour in
N(o), so lies in no Gamma triangle. Every other Gamma edge lies in exactly
one. Indicators are equivalent to ALL THREE edges being present; merely
choosing an edge decomposition into triangles would be insufficient.

Under C1, every Gamma vertex then lies in exactly five Gamma triangles.
For the 60 vertices outside any root line and its neighbourhood, each
vertex lies in at least one core triangle, and there are exactly 32-t(l)
such triangles, where t(l) is the triangle count in the cubic neighbourhood.
If c(l)=6, those 60 vertices partition into exactly twenty triangles.

More precisely t_H(w)=1+e(C[N_C(w)]). In Gamma coordinates the second
term is the sum of the four possible shared-label star edges at w and
the actual triangles at w whose other two vertices are in the two stars.
These redundant equalities expose the local triangle balance to propagation.

transport.scope:
Transport a fully fixed star, with any number and sizes of components.

    Its six pairs are already fixed by the caller's exhaustive matching
    branch. Neither a component catalogue nor the opposite matching is used.

residuals.scope:
Realize the full integer residual of a variable rotated nine-set.

For x=1_S, |S|=9, put d=(A-3I)x-1. The SRG identity gives
Ad=-4d, sum(d)=0 and ||d||^2=56-14e, where S has14+e edges.
Thus e=4 forces A1_S=1+3*1_S at EVERY vertex. For e<=2 the
same exact norm controls all99 coordinates, not just known projections.

Here S consists of an original neighbour a, four fixed Gamma vertices
and four selected Gamma corners. The old root has residual zero. The
fourteen old-neighbour coordinates are label counts, and the84 others
are adjacency sums. We also impose the fourteen old-neighbour -4
equations, which are linear in these residual coordinates.

gram.scope:
Necessary integer Gram and eigen equations for complete rotated stars.

For a new rectangle Q_ij, its nine-set residual is d_ij=-T 1_Qij,
where T^2=7T and T is the projector numerator in the new coordinates.
Consequently, for two DISTINCT rectangles,
  d_ij dot d_ik = -7 e(Q_ij,Q_ik),
  d_ij dot d_kl = 7(4-e(Q_ij,Q_kl))  when i,j,k,l are distinct.
Thus the dot products are divisible by7, nonpositive in the first case,
and at most28 in the second. Norms<=56 bound them below by-56.
Opposite-pair component identities plus incident nonpositivity also force
orthogonality between the two distinct size12 components at a line.

Optional full Gamma eigen equations impose A d=-4d at the84 original
Gamma vertices. The other15 equations already belong to the residual
model. All cuts are necessary; no adjacency or automorphism is assumed.
